notice: TEST FIXTURE — NOT a production data dependency. This file exists only so scripts/ops/sync-prod-to-qa.sh --tier=sample can choose a bounded, reproducible slice of prod to copy into the QA TEST database. Nothing in a production code path may read it. It is not an index, not a recommendation and not a redistributable dataset. Drift of a few names between refreshes is expected and acceptable; there is no freshness SLA and it must not be wired to a schedule.

equities.selection: every constituent in the article's #constituents table; the venue comes from the row's {{NyseSymbol}} / {{NasdaqSymbol}} template

etfs.source: curated large/liquid US ETFs; existence-validated against the Tiingo master
etfs.selection: curated large/liquid US ETFs across broad-market, factor, sector, international, fixed-income, commodity and leveraged categories. NOT an authoritative AUM ranking — we have no AUM source. Every ticker is verified to be a LIVE assetType=ETF row in Tiingo's master at generation time.

delisted.selection: hand-picked for FAILURE-MODE SPREAD so the cold-storage / on-request-load / 30-day-eviction path is exercised end to end. Tickers and their (exchange, listingStartDate) windows are curated; listingId, assetType and the end date are derived from Tiingo's master, and any drift aborts the generator rather than resolving to a different company.

listings.rationale: Aetna, 1977-2018, acquired by CVS. The LONGEST history in the set at ~42 years — the upper bound on cold-shard count per security.
Anadarko Petroleum, 1986-2019, acquired by Occidental. Ticker is now live again on NASDAQ from 2026 — a dead predecessor under a live ticker, which is the shape a naive bare-symbol read gets wrong.
Activision Blizzard, 1993-2023. The most RECENT delisting in the set, so its cold shards are the youngest.

Brookline Bancorp, 1998-2025. Recycled ACROSS ASSET TYPES — the live BRKL is a leveraged ETF on BATS from 2026. Named in the Candle schema as the case that defeats permaTicker, since search resolves only the current occupant.
Celgene, 1990-2019, acquired by Bristol-Myers Squibb.
Citrix Systems, 1995-2022, taken private.

Dow Chemical, 1972-2017. The canonical case: Dow Inc. holds the same ticker on the same exchange from 2019, identical in assetType and currency. A full-range read that concatenated them would return two companies as one continuous series with nothing on the row saying so.
Enron. Absent from the master and 404s on the price endpoint. Pairs with LEH: the two failures are DIFFERENT, and collapsing them is how a permanent "not there" gets retried nightly forever.
Lehman Brothers. Exists enough to answer 200 but holds no bars. The success-shaped empty response — the harder of the two to handle.
listings.upstreamBehaviour: HTTP 200 with an EMPTY array and null metadata dates

listings.rationale: LinkedIn, 2011-2016, acquired by Microsoft. The SHORTEST history at ~5.5 years — the lower bound, and the opposite extreme from AET.
Monsanto, 2000-2018. Recycled between TWO DEAD listings — a second, unrelated NASDAQ MON ran 2021-2022. Neither is live, so a "pick the active one" heuristic has nothing to pick.
Mylan, 1987-2020, combined into Viatris.
Red Hat, 1999-2019, acquired by IBM.
Raytheon, 1981-2020, merged into RTX. Long history starting on a 31 December, which is a useful year-boundary case for year-keyed cold shards.
SunTrust Banks, 1987-2019, merged into Truist. Same shape as APC with a different live successor (NASDAQ, 2024-), so the pair guards against a fix that happens to work for one of them.
Tiffany & Co., 1987-2021, acquired by LVMH. Ends in early January, so its final shard holds only a handful of bars.
Twitter, 2013-2022. Delisted by going PRIVATE rather than by merger — no successor ticker exists to fall back to.
Viacom class B, 2005-2019, recombined with CBS. A share-class ticker, so it covers the multi-class shape that GOOG/GOOGL has on the live side.
Xilinx, 1990-2022, acquired by AMD in an all-stock deal.
Yahoo!, 1996-2017. Dot-com-era listing with a long, dense history and a well-known terminal date.

funds.selection: live NMFQS assetType="Mutual Fund" USD listings. A separate vector from the equity symbols because us_fund_nav's writer (us-eod-sync leg b) selects on assetType, and the equity lists hold no funds at all — sampling that table against them matched zero rows while the run reported success. Six funds with MEASURED corporate actions are pinned first (four splits, two dividends-only as the never-split control); the remainder is filled by LISTING LONGEVITY (endDate - startDate) desc with a ticker tie-break. NOT by AUM — Tiingo's master carries no AUM and neither does mutual_fund_masters.
funds.rankedBy: listing longevity (endDate - startDate), after the pinned core
